name: Egbuta
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 2003. "Esquisse de l'egbuta, une langue en passe d'extinction au nord du Congo-Kinshasa". Studies in African Linguistics 32(2): 25-98. DOI 10.32473/sal.v32i2.107343
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 'Rudiments de phonologie' covers vowels (2.1), consonants (2.2), tone (2.3 Tonologie, pp. 43-47: H vs L plus falling/rising contour tones, tonal minimal pairs, tone rules; tonology 'du type normal', no tone displacement) and syllable structure (2.4); no mention of stress/accent d'intensité; 'accent' occurs only as the name of tone diacritics.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 2003. "Le parler budza des Yambuli (Bantou C.37)". Annales Aequatoria 24: 205-261.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Closest sister-variety sketch (Budza C.37, tagged 'phn' in Glottolog); may contain a remark on accent/prominence in Budza lects that would bear on Egbuta by proxy, though it is not an Egbuta description.

sources.citation: Van Bulck, Gaston & Peter Hackett. 1956. "Report of eastern team: Oubangui to Nile". In Linguistic Survey of the Northern Bantu Borderland, vol. 1, 63-122. London: OUP for IAI.
